evidence: universe.rs is untouched by today's three commits (`git diff --stat 32fcface~1 HEAD -- src-tauri/src/universe.rs` is empty), and line 117 still reads `let tmp = path.with_file_name(format!("{}.tmp", path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).unwrap_or("state.json")))` — a temp name derived ONLY from the target, so every concurrent writer of the same file computes the identical path. Concurrency is real, not theoretical: the callers of this helper are `#[tauri::command(async)]` (verified on save_universe_settings at universe.rs:1459 and save_universe_workspaces at 1503), so they execute on Tauri's async runtime pool, and the second screen is a separate window issuing the same commands against the same `settings.json` / `session.json` / `collections.json` / `property-types.json`. userImpact: If two Constellation windows happen to save at the same instant, your settings, your open-tab session, your collections or your list of libraries can be written as a scrambled mix of both saves — and because a scrambled file is read as empty, they silently come back blank.

userImpact: Notes you deleted can reappear in search results and link suggestions after you rename or move a folder, or the first time a library is indexed.

evidence: HEAD 6753 is `if crate::write_gate::gate_rename(source, &dest, "delete_trash").is_err() {` in `move_into_trash_folder` — the Err value is discarded with no logging and no cause discrimination, and the fallback body runs `fs::copy(source, &dest)` at 6760 (or `copy_dir_recursive` at 6756), both of which overwrite an existing destination. The premise holds on the other side too: `write_gate::gate_rename` returns `Err("An item with this name already exists at the destination.")` for a pre-existing destination at write_gate.rs:593-596, and its own comment at 589-590 says "delete_trash's `.is_err()` fallback then completes the move via copy+remove" — i.e. the never-clobber refusal is routed straight into a clobbering copy. The outside-the-lock de-collide loop at 6730-6745 is exactly the pre-check that gate_rename:582-584 documents as racy.
fixSketch: Discriminate the gate's error at 6753 — on an "already exists" refusal re-run the de-collide loop for a fresh trash name (and log the swallowed cause) instead of falling through to copy+remove.
userImpact: Deleting two files with the same name in quick succession can overwrite the first one already sitting in the trash, so it can no longer be recovered.

evidence: Read FocusPane.svelte:150-159 at HEAD: `function handleTitleKeydown(e){ if (e.key==='Enter'){e.preventDefault(); view?.focus();} if (e.key==='Escape'){ reportCaret(); onexit?.(); } }` — the Escape branch never calls `ontitlechange`. FocusPane.svelte was not touched by any of today's three commits (its last change is ca6ce954).
fixSketch: In `handleTitleKeydown`'s Escape branch, run the same commit `handleTitleBlur` does (`if (titleValue !== title) ontitlechange?.(titleValue)`) before `reportCaret()` / `onexit?.()` — ideally by calling `handleTitleBlur()` directly so there is one commit path.
userImpact: If you retype a note's title in Focus mode and press Esc to get back to writing, the new title is thrown away without a word — the note keeps its old name.

userImpact: You drag a note's review priority and the number stays where you put it, but nothing was actually saved — you only discover it later when the note is back at its old priority.

evidence: libraries.rs:559 is `#[tauri::command]` and 560 is `pub fn write_note(` — plain sync, unchanged by today's commits. Its body ends at `crate::write_gate::gate_write(path, &content, expect.as_ref(), surface)`, which takes a per-path mutex and does an fsync'd atomic write (write_gate.rs:387-397; the module's own bench at 1035-1046 measures "avg gated write (8KB, fsync incl.)"). Every other file-mutating command in the same file IS `#[tauri::command(async)]`: create_note:927, rename_item:1240, resolve_structural_conflict:2039, move_item:2089, update_links_on_rename:6018, move_to_trash:6568, delete_path:6649 (write_conflict_sidecar:619 is the one other sync straggler). The repo documents why this matters, in its own words at search.rs:11238-11240: "`(async)` moves this off the WebView2 IPC dispatch thread so a writer-lock wait … can never freeze the app." write_gate.rs:1049-1053 also notes the concurrency proofs "MUST stay green before any note-file command is converted to #[tauri::command(async)]" — the conversion is anticipated and the proofs exist.
fixSketch: Change the attribute at libraries.rs:559 to `#[tauri::command(async)]` (the body has no `.await`; gate_write already serialises per path) and run the write_gate concurrency proofs before shipping.
userImpact: When a save has to wait — a slow or synced drive, antivirus scanning the file, another write to the same note — the whole window can lock up instead of just that one save taking longer.
